messages.subject: Two Belt Methods
parts:
Hi all!
I'm analyzing some transect data obtained with the two belt method.
Birds deteected were classified just as within 25 m of distance or out
of this band.
The procedure for estimating density from this type of data are
clearly explained in the book of Bibby et al: Bird Census Techniques
(Box 4.6) but I have not found in any place the formulas for calculating
the standard error of densities estimated in this way.
I would acknowledge very much if any body can send me information
about this subject.
Best wishes
Germ=E1n L=F3pez

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: Two Belt Methods
parts:
> > I'm analyzing some transect data obtained with the two belt method.
> > Birds deteected were classified just as within 25 m of distance or out
> > of this band.

For point transects, this is given on p204-5 of the 2001 distance
sampling book. (It's also in the 1993 book.) The maths doesn't work out
so nicely for line transects - see the reference to Jarvinen and Vaisanen
on p206. For the half-normal model, you have to use numerical methods, so
the easy solution is to use Distance with 2 distance bands, giving some
upper limit for the outer band. 100m might work OK for smaller species -
try different choices, based on estimates of the maximum distance a
species is potentially detectable, and see if estimation is sensitive to
this choice.

Steve Buckland
